stemMd: According to the passage, Nan taught the narrator to work the rope chiefly by:

options.label: A
options.textMd: stopping a task herself and letting the narrator do it badly.

options.label: B
options.textMd: taking the rope back the moment the narrator made a mistake.

options.label: C
options.textMd: requiring the narrator to watch a full season of crossings before touching the rope.

options.label: D
options.textMd: talking the narrator through each step of a crossing before any attempt was allowed.

explanationMd:
The third paragraph states the method almost as a definition: "She never taught me anything directly. She would simply stop doing a thing, and wait, and I would eventually do it badly, and she would let me." Three elements are named there — she withdraws, she waits, and she allows the failure to happen. Choice A collects all three.

The incident that follows confirms it. When the narrator hauls in too fast and cracks the gunwale, Nan does not take over and does not explain; she says four words, "You will remember that," and the narrator reports, "I did." The mistake was the lesson.

Check the answer by asking, for each of the other choices, whether the passage shows Nan doing that even once. It never shows her explaining a procedure in advance, never shows her taking the rope back, and never mentions a required watching period.

distractorRationale.d: Describes ordinary step-by-step instruction, which the paragraph explicitly rules out with the sentence "She never taught me anything directly." It is the method most readers expect, which is why it is tempting.
distractorRationale.b: Turns Nan's one recorded response to a mistake into an intervention. After the gunwale is cracked she says only "You will remember that"; she does not take the rope back, and the narrator keeps working it.
distractorRationale.c: Invents a probationary period the passage never mentions. Nan "began letting me work the rope" in the summer the narrator turned twelve, with no stated requirement to observe a season first.

accessibilityText: The question asks how Nan, the narrator's grandmother, taught the narrator to operate the ferry rope, according to the third paragraph of the passage.

provenance.notes: Original item written for this bank against an original passage. Not derived from, and not a paraphrase of, any ACT-published question.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Paragraph 3 states it almost verbatim: 'She never taught me anything directly. She would simply stop doing a thing, and wait, and I would eventually do it badly, and she would let me.' B is directly contradicted ('never taught me anything directly'); C is contradicted by 'she would let me' and by her response to the cracked gunwale ('You will remember that'); D is contradicted by 'The summer I turned twelve she began letting me work the rope' with no watching requirement mentioned.

review.notes: Author solved the item and tried to defend each distractor. B is negated verbatim by "She never taught me anything directly"; C is contradicted by the gunwale incident, in which Nan does not intervene; D has no textual basis. Awaiting an independent blind solve. Options were reordered after review to remove answer-position bias; ids and labels were remapped with the key.
